name: Desktop Commander MCP
outcome_statement: As of 2026-11-14: meets C1, C2, C3, C4, C6, C9, C10; partly meets C5, C7, C8.

findings.title: Source and release provenance
findings.finding: The npm record for @wonderwhy-er/desktop-commander@0.3.3 names the repository `git+https://github.com/wonderwhy-er/DesktopCommanderMCP.git` and carries a provenance attestation (`dist.attestations`).

findings.title: Published security policy
findings.finding: GitHub shows a security policy for the repository (`SECURITY.md` in the repository), and it describes how to report a vulnerability.

findings.title: Maintenance status
findings.finding: The repository is not archived and the package is not marked deprecated. Latest release 0.3.3 is dated 2026-11-12; the newest commit on `main` is dated 2026-11-12; GitHub reports the last push on 2026-11-12.

findings.title: Published advisories
findings.finding: No advisory is published in the repository's advisory list.

findings.title: Documented scope controls
findings.finding: Terminal commands and file edits are core functions; the README documents directory and command restrictions and states their limits. Quoted: “Directory restrictions and command blocking can be bypassed through various methods including symlinks, command substitution, and absolute paths or code execution”.

findings.title: Credential handling in the documented setup
findings.finding: The documented local setup takes no API key or token. Searched `README.md` for: API_KEY, _TOKEN\b.

findings.title: Telemetry and outbound data, as documented
findings.finding: Telemetry is documented as collected by default, with a documented opt-out. The npm record declares a `postinstall` script that runs `dist/track-installation.js`. Quoted: “Desktop Commander collects limited, pseudonymous telemetry to improve the tool.”; “**Opt-out:** Ask Claude to "disable Desktop Commander telemetry" or set `"telemetryEnabled": false` in your config.”; “node dist/track-installation.js”.

findings.title: Dependency management files
findings.finding: A lockfile (`package-lock.json`) is committed. No Dependabot or Renovate configuration file exists at the paths listed in the methodology.

findings.title: Documentation of untrusted-content risk
findings.finding: The security policy names prompt injection and recommends OS-level isolation for that case. Quoted: “Desktop Commander does not protect against a compromised AI account or prompt injection reaching a trusted client. For that threat model, use OS-level isolation.”.

findings.title: Currency of the declared MCP library
findings.finding: Declared MCP library: @modelcontextprotocol/sdk ^1.32.1. Lower-bound version 1.32.1 of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk (npm) was published on 2026-10-05, within the 12 months before 2026-11-14.
